title: Characterization of valid codec bits
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $n,s\ge0$, and assign a Boolean value to every codec-bit position. This assignment satisfies the validity conditions exactly when it is the bit encoding of some row consisting of an input word of length $n$, an optional state, an input-head position among $n+2$ positions, work-tape symbols and head positions on each of $k$ tapes across $2s+1$ cells, and an output summary. The validity conditions require exactly one input-head position and state, exactly one head position per work tape, never simultaneously marking a cell as containing both Boolean symbols, and never marking both output-summary bits true.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite-state Boolean-alphabet Turing machine
